subject: Business Models
title: Forced Bundling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Forced Bundling.

hook.text: You want Hulu. Disney sells it bundled with Disney+ and ESPN+ for $13. You can't get Hulu alone cheaper.

buildup.text: Forced bundling ties the product you want to products you don't, inflating the total subscription price.

discovery.text: Microsoft 365 bundles Teams, which killed Slack's growth. Why pay for Slack when Teams is 'free' in the bundle?

twist.text: The EU forced Microsoft to unbundle Teams from Office 365 in Europe, calling it anti-competitive.

climax.text: Bundling increases average revenue per user but invites regulatory scrutiny when dominant players do it.

punchline.text: Buy what you want, get what you don't. Bundles hide the real price.

quiz.question: Why did the EU force Microsoft to unbundle Teams?
options: Anti-competitive bundling with dominant Office suite

details.summary: Forced bundling requires customers to purchase a package of features or services they may not want in order to access the ones they do. Microsoft 365 bundles Teams whether you want it or not. Streaming services bundle original content with licensed content at a single price.
details.whyItMatters: Forced bundling extracts maximum revenue per subscriber by preventing cherry-picking of high-value features. While it maximizes ARPU, it also creates resentment and competitive vulnerability if unbundled alternatives emerge.
takeaways: Customers must buy the entire package to access specific features they want
Bundling maximizes average revenue per user across diverse needs
Unbundled competitors can undercut bundles by targeting specific needs

faq.question: Why do companies force bundles instead of offering modular pricing?
faq.answer: Bundles capture maximum willingness to pay across diverse customer needs. A customer wanting only one feature still pays for the full bundle. The total bundle price can exceed what any customer would pay for their individually desired features alone, maximizing revenue per subscriber.

faq.question: When does forced bundling create competitive vulnerability?
faq.answer: When a focused competitor offers the most desired feature at a lower price, luring away customers who only wanted that specific feature. Slack challenged Microsoft Teams this way. Spotify challenged music bundled within Apple's ecosystem. Unbundling is the classic disruptive strategy.
